A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GDN-CC research, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. V1's large-corpus appendix is incorporated into v3's main text, while its prompts remain in the renamed Appendix G.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation analyses, trained-model evaluations, clarification comparisons, and clustering experiments in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds encoder-extraction results, clustering metrics, and quantitative clarification-error findings.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2.1 adds encoder alternatives for AU extraction: BIO token classification and direct span classification, with different losses and decoding procedures. This extends one stage of the retained three-step framework; the existing AS encoder and generative clarification procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same French consultation, four themes, 1,231 manually annotated contributions, and 239,798 automatically annotated contributions. The extraction, structure-detection, clarification, and clustering tasks are retained. V3's proposed future encoder-generated corpus is not a newly evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The AU-extraction comparison gains encoder approaches alongside the retained GPT-4.1, Llama, Mistral, Qwen, and Gemma models. The AS encoder was already evaluated in v1; its appearance in v3's Table 2 is a redistribution of existing comparison evidence.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 replaces raw AS-label agreement with Cohen's kappa and class F1, and Section 6.5 adds silhouette and Davies–Bouldin clustering metrics. The new AU encoders introduce their own training and validation-selection protocols. The 70/15/15 split remains unchanged, and UMAP/HDBSCAN were already specified in v1's Appendix F.

E4.justification: V3 documents a 100-output Gemma clarification audit with four error categories, extending v1's qualitative mitigation claim and examples. Appendix C.2.1 also compares BIO and span formulations qualitatively for performance and computational cost. Existing annotation-correction analyses and examples remain.

E5.justification: The Beta quality-estimation procedure and the chi-square and binomial significance tests in Appendices D–F are retained. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added. The new agreement and clustering scores change evaluation metrics rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results expand across several central evaluations. The new AU encoder achieves micro/macro F1 of 0.823/0.831 in Table 11, exceeding the retained Qwen scores of 0.75/0.81. V3 adds clustering scores of 0.46 versus 0.59 for silhouette and 0.48 versus 0.46 for Davies–Bouldin, Gemma error frequencies, and correction proportions in Table 8. Figure 8 also changes, including the twice-labeled solution proportion from 43% to 36%. Existing decoder scores and LLM-judge preference counts remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2.1 adds the formal BIO label mapping and token-probability specification for the new AU encoder. The existing AS span representation is restated compactly, while its loss and decoding mathematics and Appendix D's Beta likelihood remain unchanged. No new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion extends the claim that finetuned SLMs match or outperform large proprietary models to include finetuned encoders. The abstract's principal claims about Corpus Clarification, GDN-CC, and GDN-CC-large remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 characterizes AS agreement as moderate using kappa and interprets residual Gemma errors as mainly oversimplification, arguing that these are less concerning than invented justifications. The existing limitations concerning language coverage, prompting, contributor voice, and dependence on private models remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds experiment-code access information, links to a collection covering datasets and models, and updates the annotation-platform repository location. Appendix C.2.1 supplies AU-encoder implementation and training details, including learning rate 2×10^-5, dropout 0.1, and batch size 4. The older AS-encoder settings are retained.

R1.justification: Related Work adds Key Point Analysis through Friedman et al. (2021) and earlier argumentative-unit segmentation through Ajjour et al. (2017). Additional references support agreement and clustering metrics, while the BERTopic citation is removed. The broader research positioning remains stable; the BERTScore publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to agreement and experiment passages, Related Work headings, the subdivision of Appendix C.2, relocation of the large-corpus discussion, and new acknowledgments. Most prose remains intact. V3 also introduces an empty Section 6.4 heading.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains an encoder column, Table 8 gains a correction-proportion row, and Tables 10–11 present the new AU encoder. V1's large-corpus Table 14 moves into the main text as Table 3, and Figure 1 is redrawn with the same pipeline. Existing screenshots and decoder-result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens validation through encoder comparisons, chance-corrected agreement, and clustering metrics independent of an LLM judge, while improving code and model access information. These are useful but bounded gains. The new 19% GPT-4.1 versus 2% Gemma over-analysis comparison has unclear comparable sampling and denominators relative to Table 8, limiting the strength of that particular conclusion.
